tasks.title: Use Exception when a site task has no contract system
tasks.about: The intake is not expert yet. If a job cannot be matched to a contract system, put Exception in the System column and show the row in red. If it can be matched, keep that system (Drainage, Lighting, and so on). The user can change the system afterwards.

tasks.title: Let the user correct the system on a site task
tasks.about: The detected system is sometimes wrong. On each row, let the user change the system.

tasks.title: Add a site task by hand
tasks.about: The parser sometimes skips a task that is written in the report. Let the user add a task themselves, with description, system, classification, source, and date.

tasks.title: Filter the site-task list
tasks.about: Filter the list by system, classification, source, and date.

tasks.title: WhatsApp is pasted like a site report, for now
tasks.about: The client asked how to attach WhatsApp. For now it is the same as a site report: paste the messages, and add photos with the photo field. They had also pictured attaching the site report as a file, and connecting the system to a WhatsApp group or contact. They are willing to try the paste flow first. A live WhatsApp connection is not part of this round.

tasks.title: Open Calculation Sheets filtered by the row's system
tasks.about: Clicking the system on a site-task row opens Calculation Sheets with the list filtered to that system.

tasks.title: Show the BOQ Manual badge on the quantity-check list
tasks.about: Manual means the same purple Manual badge already shown next to the section number on BOQ Items (items that have a manual concentration entry). On the Check quantities list, show that same badge next to every such item number. The client searched for 'manual' on BOQ Items and pointed at those badges.

tasks.title: Hide manual items and non-BOQ items from the quantity check
tasks.about: Give separate options to hide items that carry the BOQ Manual badge, and to hide non-BOQ items, from the Check quantities list.

tasks.title: Open the Concentration sheet from a quantity-check row
tasks.about: Clicking an item in the Check quantities list opens that item's Concentration sheet.

tasks.title: Keep the quantity-check list open across pages
tasks.about: The mismatch list should stay visible when the user goes to other sheets, so they can work through the errors. Give a way to close it.

tasks.title: Show which non-BOQ items were moved to a new project
tasks.about: The usual action sends all non-BOQ items to one new project, but some items must be left out. After an item is sent, show a check on that row in the original project's list. Rows that were not sent stay unmarked.

tasks.title: Link the new project back to the project it came from
tasks.about: When a new project is created from non-BOQ items, remember the main project it came from and show that link. The client asked if this is possible. It is.

tasks.title: Copy the related calculation sheets into the new project
tasks.about: A calculation sheet often contains both contract items and non-BOQ items. The new project receives only the non-BOQ items from those sheets. Those sheets must already appear under Calculation Sheets in the new project, ready to use.

tasks.title: Keep the Dashboard non-BOQ list closed until opened
tasks.about: The Non-BOQ list on the Dashboard currently opens expanded, and the long list is in the way. Keep it closed until the user opens it. The client marked the list header in the screenshot.

tasks.title: Print calculation sheets the way Excel prints them
tasks.about: Confirmed. Print only the block of cells that have data on the Calculation sheet, right to left, the way the Excel file is laid out. Landscape or portrait and the margins stay as choices. Do not print the empty grid. Hebrew must read in the right direction, and quantities must not show junk decimals such as 13.850000000000001.

tasks.title: Find an element from concentration descriptions
tasks.about: The drawing-list Element column is often empty for now, and when it is filled it holds the element name or another name. The names to use today are in the concentration sheet Description and Work Description columns. Example: section 1.02.01.0736 has entries DC-36 and DC-02 in Description, and the same names inside the Work Description. For a chosen element, show its contract items and which of them have been submitted.
